{"completeness": 0.65, "citation_quality": 0.5, "severity_defensibility": 0.75, "overall_pass": false, "feedback": "The investigation appropriately downgrades severity based on lack of corroborating auth logs, which is defensible given the evidence. However, completeness is weakened by poor ATT&CK citation—T1110 Brute Force and T1621 MFA Request Generation are not supported by the investigation findings (no MFA challenges or brute force detected), and the analyst should have instead focused on T1078 Valid Accounts as the primary technique with reasoning about why credential compromise is or isn't indicated. Citation quality suffers because the three techniques aren't justified by the actual investigation narrative. Additionally, while the investigation correctly notes the absence of corroborating logs, it should more explicitly address whether this absence itself is concerning (e.g., could logs have been deleted or is the tool integration working properly), and should clarify whether the 127-minute travel time being \"physically plausible\" truly dismisses the alert or if other factors (account history, typical travel patterns) matter. Recommend: (1) revise ATT&CK techniques to only T1078 with clear justification about why the impossible travel pattern—even if physically possible—warrants this classification, (2) explicitly state whether the lack of logs is expected or anomalous for this account, and (3) consider whether \"no evidence of breach\" should be confidence ~0.2 or higher given the absence of supporting data."}
